examples.signature: Compare scalp EEG and an intracortical microelectrode array for the same motor-interface goal without declaring one universally superior
Trace an assistive motor BCI from neural activity through sensing, acquisition, decoding, device control, feedback, and user adaptation
Classify a cochlear implant as a sensory neuroprosthesis that encodes external sound into patterned stimulation rather than as a device that simply amplifies sound
Contrast open-loop stimulation with a closed-loop system that senses a biomarker and adapts therapy while preserving explicit safety constraints
Sort representative technologies into recording, modulation, restoration, rehabilitation, or augmentation goals while allowing one platform to serve more than one role
Classify a fingertip sensory pathway simultaneously by anatomical location (PNS/CNS), information direction (afferent), and functional organization (somatic sensory)
Map withdrawal from a hot surface through peripheral sensory input, spinal integration, somatic motor output, and ascending pathways to show that the spinal cord is not merely a relay cable
Compare cortex, spinal cord, peripheral nerve, and muscle as four possible interface locations for the same hand-movement restoration objective
Contrast somatic efferent control of wrist extension with autonomic efferent control of heart rate to separate efferent from voluntary
Map a cochlear implant from external sound through encoded stimulation, auditory nerve activity, brainstem and higher CNS pathways, perception, and behavioral adaptation

Trace one simplified motor neuron across soma-proximal, axonal, peripheral-nerve, and downstream-muscle observation sites to show that one pathway produces different measured signals at different biological levels
Use two ionic compartments separated by a potassium-selective membrane to build qualitative intuition for competing concentration and electrical forces
Contrast intracellular inside-versus-outside membrane-voltage measurement with extracellular field recording produced by transmembrane ionic currents
Compare similarly sized myelinated and unmyelinated axons to show why glial myelin changes propagation dynamics, recording timing, and stimulation recruitment

Trace one stored microvolt-scale digital sample backward through amplifier, electrode, electrode-tissue interface, extracellular field, transmembrane current, channel states, and metabolically maintained ion gradients
